purpose: Freeze what is now established about the NASA/NSSDC sounding-rocket source lineage, and explicitly prevent a visually fragmented full-text extraction from being promoted into a row-complete event manifest before deterministic row validation exists.

catalog_schema_probe.documented_rocket_id_rule: UT launch date plus a unique sequential two-digit serial number

established_source_semantics.catalog_population: Scientifically successful rockets identified by WDC-A/NSSDC; this is a positive-event population, not an all-attempt or no-launch denominator.
native_system: NSSDC operated a machine-sensible ROCKET information system.
The central rocket-flight index was maintained on magnetic tape.
ROCKET files supported update routines and select/sort operations.
Selections could be made on ROCKET entries except the remarks section.
Two standard listings containing much of the file content on all rockets were prepared monthly; one was sorted by NSSDC rocket ID and the other by agency ID.
A complete file listing was prepared periodically for internal NSSDC use.
WDC-A published a monthly Sounding Rocket Launching Report (SRL) containing successful rocket/experiment entries added to the file.

current_extraction_diagnostic.representation: Official NTRS plain-text extraction of the 1972 catalogue
current_extraction_diagnostic.observation: The prose/schema portions are readable, but the wide launch listing is fragmented into many short table-cell/column lines rather than one stable launch per textual row.
current_extraction_diagnostic.strong_signal: The frozen schema probe found 227812 total text lines and a median nonempty line length of only 2 characters, consistent with a highly fragmented table extraction.
current_extraction_diagnostic.consequence: A date-token regex can locate candidate cells, but cannot by itself establish correct row assembly, neighboring rocket/site fields, duplicate handling, or row completeness.

required_before_any_new_bluebook_or_poss: Freeze a deterministic official row-oriented representation or a deterministic reconstruction whose row grouping is validated against an official row-oriented output/example.
Every admitted event row must bind at minimum launch date, rocket/agency identity where present, launch site or site code where present, and source locator/provenance.
Demonstrate deterministic row count and duplicate policy for the frozen study-window extraction.
Demonstrate that parser output is stable under replay from the same frozen source bytes.
Keep NASA catalogue semantics positive-event-only; absence of a parsed row must never become NO_ROCKET or a negative control.
Freeze event manifest and parser receipt before any Blue Book/POSS temporal or spatial outcome join.
acceptable_source_routes: Public NSSDC/WDC-A native or derivative machine-readable rocket file/listing.
Public monthly Sounding Rocket Launching Report issues with deterministic row schema and adequate coverage for the target interval.
A separately frozen official representation that preserves row geometry sufficiently to validate the NTRS text reconstruction.
not_acceptable: Manual hand-picked launch dates as a replacement for the catalogue population.
Treating extraction gaps as no-launch days.
Guessing table rows by proximity alone in the fragmented TXT without a validation certificate.
Using Blue Book/POSS outcomes to tune row grouping, date parsing, launch-site selection, or inclusion rules.

119l_parallel_boundary.rule: 119L daily counts/dates remain blocked until an official companion row source is frozen; operational limits and the aggregate 184 launches may not be interpolated into daily rows.

next_actions: Search official NTRS/NSSDCA descendants for the standard monthly ROCKET listings, Sounding Rocket Launching Report, or preserved machine-readable output from the NSSDC ROCKET system.
Search official NSSDC data-listing / master-directory lineage for an identifier or access path to the ROCKET system product.
For 119L, continue official AFCRC/ARDC/1110th ASG companion-record search for Tab M Statistics / IBM Machine Run or another row-level flight manifest.
If no public row-oriented descendant is found, retain the NASA catalogue as source/schema evidence and positive-event locator only; do not manufacture a complete manifest.
